headline: First aid bridges the gap—basic skills to stabilize until professional help arrives
universal_truth: Being able to help beats standing helpless; basic competence in emergencies empowers action
fun_facts: CPR can double or triple survival chances when performed immediately after cardiac arrest
The first few minutes after injury are often the most critical for outcome
Simple actions like applying pressure to a wound can be lifesaving
discussion_questions: Would you know what to do if someone near you was injured?
What basic skills would make you more useful in an emergency?
Why do many people freeze when help is needed?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Someone collapses. Someone's bleeding. Someone's choking. In those moments, help might be minutes away—but seconds matter. First aid is what you can do now, before professionals arrive. It's the bridge between emergency and expert care.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Most emergencies happen around regular people, not paramedics. Why is basic first aid knowledge so important?

options.text: First aid fills the critical gap—professionals aren't immediately present, so untrained bystanders often determine outcomes in the first crucial minutes
options.response: Yes. Ambulances take minutes. Brain damage from oxygen deprivation starts in four. The gap between emergency and expert help is often filled by whoever is there. Be capable.

options.text: First aid is just for serious injuries
options.response: Serious injuries especially, but even minor injuries benefit from proper initial response...

q1.title: Bridge the Gap
q1.script: First aid isn't treatment—it's stabilization. Stop the bleeding. Clear the airway. Keep them breathing. Buy time until real help arrives. The goal is maintaining life, not curing.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Bridge the Gap"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Simple Actions Matter
q2.script: Complex medical procedures require training. But the most important first aid is often simple: apply pressure, call for help, don't move someone with spinal injury. Simple knowledge saves lives.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Overcoming Freeze
q3.script: Many people freeze in emergencies—they want to help but don't know how. Basic training replaces helplessness with action. Knowing what to do enables doing it.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Being able to help beats standing helpless. Basic competence in emergencies empowers action. Learn the basics.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 312. Tomorrow, we'll explore avoiding things going wrong—prevention. Until then, consider whether you'd know what to do in an emergency.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: First Aid Assessment - Could You Help?
growTrack.learning_objective: Assess emergency readiness and plan training
growTrack.activity: If someone near you had a medical emergency right now, what would you do? Do you know CPR? How to stop bleeding? Consider taking a basic first aid course. Being prepared beats being helpless.
